items.title: Prioritise, categorise and share To Do list
items.summary: I'm looking for a way of creating a To Do list. There are 4 of us in my team and each person will have a list of tasks. I want to set a priority and category to each task and have each assigned to one of us. I'd like to be able to see all tasks in a single list and also be able to filter them by team member, priority and category. Ideally, I'd like to be able to add notes in an individual task. I could do it in Excel but wondered if there is any software that does it out of the box. Also, I work for the health service and paid software won't be an option unfortunately. Thanks.

items.title: Open-source Google Keep alternatives?
items.summary: Is there any comparable alternative to Google's Keep? Features I require: notes must support including images (via copy and paste) and other files (PDFs) and treat them as attachments/image gallery, not necessarily inline (because there may be many images/large images) notes, images and PDFs must be indexed/searchable (via OCR (ie easyocr)) I wrote a note taking app with integrated live search ( https://github.com/jjYBdx4IL/ajax-solnotes ), but abandoned it because Google Keep does perfect OCR on images, which I can just copy and paste into notes there.

items.title: GUI for editing multiple JSON files
items.summary: I am looking to edit JSON files in bulk / batch. I know I can do this programmatically, or do find/replaces across files, but I am hoping to find a friendlier GUI that allows me to do things across a selection of files like: editing a certain key: adding a key nice to have: seeing stats of the value of a specific key to quickly spot typo's Is there something available like this for any OS, or as a webapp?

items.title: Meal planning app with grocery list and custom meal types
items.summary: I am looking for a meal planner application Features: adding my own recipies defining meals for each week day, e.g., tom yam soup on Friday lunch generating grocery list from the ingredients defined meals defining meal types: breakfast, second breakfast, lunch, etc. Target platform : Windows or online Paid versions : I am fine if the application is not free. What would you recommend? I have found Paprika , but version for Windows does not offer defining meal types.

items.title: Lookin for the Best Battery App
items.summary: Mainly to alert me when my battery is critically low

items.title: Free software to record webcam on Windows that will keep recording in background and even if the computer in locked
items.summary: Please recommend me a free software that can record video from webcam on a Windows computer. I have tried ScreenToGif to record from webcam but it requires the program to be in foreground. If it is minimized or you open another window or lock the computer, it won't record the webcam. So my requirement is a program what will keep recording in background (i.e. with other windows or programs in forefront, e.g. a browser) and even if the computer in locked.

items.title: How to Transfer Photos from iCloud Photos to Google Drive
items.summary: I'm looking for a convenient way to transfer photos from iCloud Photos to Google Drive. I have photos stored in my Apple account and want to move a copy of them to Google Drive so I can access and manage them more easily across different devices. I've been exploring different options, including downloading photos from iCloud and uploading them manually, but that can become time-consuming when dealing with a large photo library. I also came across All Cloud Hub , a multi-cloud management platform available as a web app and mobile apps for iOS and Android.

items.title: What software can help me organize and manage personal files stored across multiple cloud storage services?
items.summary: I'm looking for software that can help me manage personal files stored across multiple cloud storage services from one place. My main requirements are: Unified file management: Browse and organize files from different cloud storage accounts. Easy file access: Access documents, photos, and other personal files without repeatedly switching between services. File synchronization: Keep selected folders synchronized across devices. Security: Support secure account access and protect personal files. Backup support: Make it easier to maintain copies of important files.

items.title: Does anyone know of a SwiftUI compiler?
items.summary: I do not want something big to download, like Xcode, but I want an online SwiftUI compiler that I can open from my browser.

items.title: Apache/Nginx log file analysis tool that allows drilling down to individual URLs with web UI
items.summary: I'm aware of things like AWStats and GoAccess, but neither of them really provide quite what I'm looking for in a logfile analysis tool. Basically, it seems to me that it should be relatively simple to regularly parse access logfiles, stick them in a SQLite database, and allow a web interface to be pretty flexible based on being able to query that DB. For instance, if I have a panel showing a list of different URLs retrieved by number of hits, I may want to click on one and drill down to see a graph over time of just that URL.

items.title: Transfer Proxmox raw disk to Hyper-V
items.summary: I run several Proxmox in my lab. Now I want to play with Hyper-V and avoid creating virtual machines from scratch. Can you recommend any tools for raw to VHDX conversion?

items.title: What software can help manage large volumes of data for long-term archiving?
items.summary: I'm researching ways to manage large volumes of historical business data while keeping storage organized, secure, and accessible when needed. I'm interested in data archiving software that can help with long-term retention without requiring all archived information to remain on expensive, high-performance storage. My main requirements are: Scalability: The solution should accommodate growing volumes of files and records. Retention management: It should support configurable retention policies.

items.title: Multiple monitors slideshow
items.summary: The people in my department and I are stumped about a good program that will manage our multiple monitors. All we really want to do is have a slideshow run. The problem it seems is that most of the solutions we find are cumbersome or only manage a few monitors. We have 5 monitors. Each are oriented landscape wise but are positioned vertically next to each other. Ideally, we'd run a slide show. Each of the 5 monitors would run a group of slides and then switch to the next group of five. Does anyone know of software that will meet our needs? Obviously googling has gotten us nowhere.

items.title: Automation software for Android application
items.summary: I'm looking for a free software to automate a procedure with an Android Application. At the moment i'm using UIPath (community edition) along with Bluestacks (Android emulator software for gaming), but designing scripts to automate what I'm trying to accomplish seems to be a little tricky. Plus, Bluestacks comes rooted and, since the device would be under MDM, this isn't an option, because rooting the device would make it non-compliant. Specifically, I'm trying to automate a procedure for daily reservation in an application I already have.

items.title: Does an EFI subshell, that produces a videographic replay of all entered commands, and their output, exist?
items.summary: I want to be able to capture a screencast of an EFI shell without purchasing hardware, like a (DP or HDMI) capture device. This is already possible outside such a shell, as github.com/charmbracelet/vhs ASCIINemia demonstrates. The sole alternative is creating something like what superuser.com/q/520086 explains. However, that's even less feasible in such a basic shell, and I want it as a video.

items.title: software for storing, browsing, tagging, and cataloging visual reference and inspiration material
items.summary: GD student here, figuring some stuff out about how to store, tag, and efficiently browse reference material, for inspiration and context, solely offline , so no browser apps, and I use Win11. I have recently started out reading a few books from my library about graphic design and its history, and there are a lot of references to and depictions of works of art and artists, respectively, which I then decided to have a personal gallery or museum of, so that I can reference them, building a visual library of sorts.

items.title: Does any software provide a graphical interface to sign text with an SSH key?
items.summary: KGPG (and, I believe, Kleopatra) provide an interface that allows me to conveniently sign arbitrary text with an enumerated PGP key. Does anything provide this for ssh-keygen -Y sign ? I ask due to what community.bitwarden.com/t/79185/2 describes: Bitwarden supports storing and providing SSH keys. I store my SSH keys inside Bitwarden. Bitwarden does not support PGP. I am not particularly worried about the apparent lack of SSH key-servers, considering that gitlab.com/api/v4/users/7984176/keys verifies mine.

items.title: How to separate human from non-human visits in webserver access logs?
items.summary: I need to perform usage analysis on a few websites based on no more than standard access logs, e.g. Apache's access_log . Entries have a timestamp, a URL path, a client IP address, a HTTP status, and a few more bits, but no USER_AGENT or HTTP_REFERER . Most of the sites are low-volume, so the majority of visits is from bots: crawlers from search engine operators, SEO optimizers, vulnerability scanners, etcetera. Such automated visits must be excluded from the analysis as much as possible. 100% accuracy isn't required, but 90% would be nice. Are any tools or resources available for doing this?

items.title: One static docs site from OpenAPI, MCP, and Doxygen specs?
items.summary: I need to build a self-hosted documentation site for a small API project. My specs are a mix: an OpenAPI file, an MCP server, some C code with Doxygen comments, and plain Markdown. I want one static HTML site generated from all of it, hosted on my own server. It should be open source and run from the command line. What tools can do this in 2026?

items.title: png image viewer that shows tEXt metadata
items.summary: I am looking for a simple image viewer for PNGs that also displays the metadata encoded within the image (png tEXt chunks). It needs to: support most PNG image types (but MUST support viewing 16bit grayscale ). show the standard tEXt chunks (from png spec; Title, Author, Description, etc). show non-standard tEXt chunks in the file (bonus if it also displays iTxt and zTxt as well). run on Windows 7 and up (but even better if its cross-platform). be free for personal use (but even better if its open source).

items.title: Library or tool for programmatic 3D model generation
items.summary: I'm currently developing a tool, that allows users to generate simple textured 3D models given an image and some dimensions as input values. Using these I need to generate some simple geometric shapes with a material based on that texture. This is currently limited to cuboids, but I'd like to keep the option to generate more complicated shapes in the future. The resulting files then need to be exported in glb format. The service is currently written in Golang and I use a gltf library to manually generate the resulting files.

items.title: Project tracking/supervision
items.summary: I need to track/supervise the progress of a number of simple projects (about 50 at a time). I need an overview of all current projects (active and pending). In short, I need to know to whom I have assigned a certain task, which project does that task belong in, what the task is and when that person is due to finish it. The software is for my use only – no team members involved and I don't need collaboration software. The projects are linear (never more than one task pending and never more than one person working on it). The status of the projects changes daily, often several times per day.

items.title: Countdown, Timer & Alarm Clock software with very specific features

Desired features: (Not in order of priority, that comes later) Main: Alarm Clock : Multiple alarms Repeat function (Daily, Weekly, Weekdays, Thursdays etc.) Countdown : You set either a a) period (say 4hrs), or b) deadline (clock time AND/OR date) <-- Can be an extension of the "Alarm" feature.

That is, in addition to just setting up the environment, I want to be able to call some batch file that in turn also further configures the environment. First I want to note that I haven't lost my mind and made up a problem for myself — this is, in my view, a real problem.

items.title: Anthropic should give stock to Stack Overflow (and OpenAI too)

items.title: Do LLMs really code better than you?
items.summary: I keep seeing this sentiment in the comments on here from supposed 25 year storied career programmers. I’ve been programming for 14ish years professionally and can say for a fact an agent doesn’t code better than I do. I’ve used the latest models and even with heavy steering the code it produces is not subjectively or un subjectively “better”. It is more verbose, more defensive, has more comments, it’s done faster. The fact someone I highly respect that uses the agentic workflow effectively told me to “stop being so precious about the code” makes it obvious to me that both can’t be true.

items.title: Tool: Kiri
items.summary: Docker Desktop alternative. What we like: Single, Docker-compatible daemon (CLI, Compose, buildx). Performance optimized with a small memory footprint. Includes networks, volumes, k8s. Dev tools like auto-HTTPs endpoints with publicly sharable URLs. Supports macOS, Windows, Linux. What we dislike: Non-native UI, unlike something like Orbstack (which is macOS only). “Machines” are containers with filesystem access, not true VMs.

items.title: Tool: Jiff
items.summary: Datetime library for Rust. What we like: Understands timezones natively and handles daylight sayings. Built-in handling of common date operations like durations, differences, calculations, geo regions. Uses Rust-native formatting and display options, including friendly formats. What we dislike: Shows you how complex dates and times actually are, but that probably means fewer bugs!
